sections.md:
### Carbon-Intensity Approval Deadline — December 31, 2025

FACT: "A carbon intensity determined in accordance with any of sections 76 to 79 that was approved by the Minister before July 1, 2024 ceases to be valid on December 31, 2025. The registered creator, carbon-intensity contributor or foreign supplier may, on or after July 1, 2024, submit a new application to the Minister for the approval of the carbon intensity under subsection 80(1)." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 86(9), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Registered creators and foreign suppliers whose CI approvals were granted before July 1, 2024 faced a reapplication obligation, with approved CIs expiring December 31, 2025. Workspaces acting for or alongside such entities should confirm whether new approvals were obtained and whether credit-creation capacity was interrupted.

MONITORING — Re-check: Q1 2026 to confirm reapproval status for relevant fuel suppliers.

### Fuel LCA Model Version Updates — Ongoing

*Analytical inference:* Given the pattern of Model v3.1 (December 2024) and v4.0 (January 2025) releases, further model updates are likely in 2025–2026 as ECCC refines pathway calculations for emerging fuels (sustainable aviation fuel, co-processed fuels, hydrogen). Workspaces should monitor ECCC's Fuel LCA Model publication page for updates. Specific dates not announced in corpus sources as of this brief's generation date.

MONITORING — Re-check: quarterly via ECCC Fuel LCA Model publication page.

### Rail Electrification as New Eligible Credit Activity (2025)

FACT: Version 4.0 of the Fuel LCA Model "recognized rail electrification as an eligible credit-generating activity beginning in 2025." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Operational implication:* Workspaces with rail-mode activity on Canadian corridors — or clients operating electrified rail — should assess whether credit-creation through rail electrification is available and whether registration as a registered creator is warranted for 2025 compliance periods.

---

### Primary Supplier Registration

FACT: "A primary supplier must register with the Minister by submitting a registration report to the Minister that contains the information referred to in sections 1 to 3 of Schedule 3 no later than 45 days after the day on which they have produced in Canada or imported into Canada, during a compliance period, a total volume of 400 m³ or more of gasoline or a total volume of 400 m³ or more of diesel." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 10(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "If there are any changes in the information referred to in section 1 of Schedule 3 that is provided in the registration report, the primary supplier must send a notice to the Minister that provides the updated information within 30 days after the day on which the change occurs." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 10(3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Registered Creator Registration

FACT: A person who wishes to create compliance credits may register by submitting to the Minister a registration report containing information from s. 1 of Schedule 3 and applicable information from ss. 4–12 of Schedule 3. "A registered creator must not create provisional compliance credits under subsection 19(1) or section 20 until the day after the day on which they become a registered creator." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 25(1), 25(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Reporting Obligations by Report Type

FACT: **Annual Credit-Creation Report (s. 120):** A registered creator producing credits under s. 19(1)(a), subparagraph 19(1)(d)(i)/(ii)/(iv)/(v), or s. 20(a) must submit to the Minister, no later than April 30 of the calendar year following the compliance period.

FACT: **Quarterly Credit-Creation Reports (s. 121):** A registered creator producing credits under s. 19(1)(b)/(c), subparagraph 19(1)(d)(iii), or s. 20(b)/(c) must submit quarterly reports with deadlines of: June 30 (Q1), September 30 (Q2), December 31 (Q3), and March 31 of the following year (Q4) of the compliance period.

FACT: **Credit-Adjustment Report (s. 122):** Due no later than June 30 of the year following the compliance period.

FACT: **Carbon-Intensity-Pathway Report (s. 123):** Due no later than April 30 following each compliance period in which an approved CI is in use. Applicable from compliance periods ending on or after January 1, 2024.

FACT: **Material Balance Report (s. 124):** Due no later than April 30 following each compliance period, for fuels produced using eligible feedstocks referred to in s. 46(1)(b) or (c). Applicable from compliance periods ending on or after January 1, 2024.

FACT: **Compliance Report (s. 127):** A registered primary supplier must submit, no later than July 31 following each compliance period, a compliance report. Applicable from compliance periods ending on or after July 1, 2023.

FACT: **Complementary Compliance Report (s. 128):** A registered primary supplier that has not satisfied total reduction requirements by July 31 must submit a complementary compliance report no later than December 15 following the compliance period.

*Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 120–128, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Verification Obligations

FACT: "A report or application that is referred to in either section 130 or 131 is ineligible if it is not verified in accordance with the requirements set out in sections 132 to 154." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 129, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: Applications for carbon-intensity approval under ss. 80(1) and 91(1) must be verified by a verification body where the application is in respect of a CI determined under ss. 76–79, with the verification obligation not applying to applications made before June 30, 2024. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 130(1)-(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: Nine verification bodies were registered as of May 31, 2024. *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

### Record Retention

FACT: "A person who is required by these Regulations to record information or keep it up to date, submit a report or plan or send a notice must retain a record of the information or copy of the report, plan or notice, as the case may be, as well as any supporting documents, for a period of 10 years after the day on which the information is recorded or updated, the report or plan is submitted or the notice is sent." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 166(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "A foreign supplier, primary supplier, carbon-intensity contributor or registered creator who is required under subsection (1) or (3) to retain any information or documents, including supporting documents, must keep the information and documents at their principal place of business in Canada or at another place in Canada where they may be inspected." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 166(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Workspaces maintaining records outside Canada on behalf of foreign suppliers or registered creators face a specific statutory requirement to keep those records at a Canadian principal place of business or an accessible Canadian location. Remote or cloud-based records management requires confirmation against this geographic requirement.

---

### ACTION REQUIRED — Determine Primary Supplier Status for Fuel Imports

**Action:** Engage legal counsel to confirm whether any import activity — specifically any volume of gasoline or diesel brought into Canada on behalf of clients or the workspace — meets the statutory definition of "primary supplier" under s. 1(1).

FACT: "A primary supplier who produces in Canada or imports into Canada a volume of less than 400 m³ of gasoline or a volume of less than 400 m³ of diesel during a compliance period is exempt from the application of these Regulations with respect to that fuel for that compliance period." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 4(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Workspaces involved in fuel logistics at volumes exceeding 400 m³ per compliance period face registration, volumetric, and reduction-requirement obligations — not merely cost pass-through from supplier adjustments. The 400 m³ threshold applies per fuel type (gasoline separately from diesel) and per compliance period.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether importing fuel on behalf of a client, under agency arrangements or as freight forwarder, constitutes "imports gasoline or diesel into Canada" for the purposes of the primary-supplier definition requires counsel review specific to contract structure.

**Deadline:** Registration is required no later than 45 days after the day on which a primary supplier has produced in Canada or imported into Canada a total volume of 400 m³ or more of gasoline or diesel during a compliance period (s. 10(1)).

---

### COST ALERT — Carbon-Intensity Reduction Costs Are Escalating Annually to 2030

**Action:** Map fuel procurement and logistics cost structures for Canadian operations to identify where CFR compliance credit costs are already being passed through by fuel suppliers.

FACT: The carbon-intensity limit for gasoline in the 2023 compliance period was 91.5 gCO₂e/MJ, and for diesel 89.5 gCO₂e/MJ; these limits decline annually: gasoline reaches 81.0 gCO₂e/MJ and diesel 79.0 gCO₂e/MJ in 2030 and after. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 5(1) Table, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: The baseline carbon intensity of gasoline is 95 gCO₂e/MJ and the baseline carbon intensity of diesel is 93 gCO₂e/MJ (as set out in s. 5(3)). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 5(3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: The credit clearance ceiling price is "the amount determined by the formula $300 × (CPI_A ÷ CPI_B)" where CPI_A is the average Consumer Price Index for the calendar year to which the compliance period relates and CPI_B is the average CPI for the 12 months of 2022. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 112(3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Analytical inference:* FACT: The average credit price for 2023 was CAD $127 per credit; for 2024 the average credit price was CAD $157 per credit; prices reached CAD $166 in Q2 2024 before decreasing to CAD $149.24 by Q4 2024. *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Operational implication:* As the annual reduction requirement deepens (3.5 gCO₂e/MJ in 2023, escalating 1.5 gCO₂e/MJ per year to 14 gCO₂e/MJ in 2030), primary suppliers' per-litre compliance costs rise. Workspaces procuring road fuel in Canada for fleet operations or paying fuel surcharges on Canadian freight should anticipate accelerating pass-through costs through 2030.

---

### MONITORING — Compliance Fund and Deferral Mechanism Create Backstop Pricing

**Action:** Verify whether fuel supplier contracts include provisions referencing the Compliance Fund or credit clearance mechanism, which set effective price ceilings on credit purchases.

FACT: "A Compliance Fund provides a backstop permitting purchase of up to 10% of total obligations at CAD $350 per credit." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

FACT: Contributions to a registered emission-reduction funding program create compliance credits at a rate where "the number of compliance credits that the primary supplier may create under subsection (1) for a compliance period is determined by the formula C ÷ P where C is the amount of the primary supplier's contribution to the registered emission-reduction funding program; and P is $350," with P indexed to CPI annually. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 118(3)-(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

---

### 12A. Primary Supplier Exemption — Below 400 m³

FACT: Exemption applies per fuel type (gasoline, diesel) per compliance period for volumes below 400 m³. Volumes of excluded fuels (aviation gasoline, exports, competition fuels, research fuels) are not counted toward the 400 m³ threshold. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 4(1), 4(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 12B. Newfoundland and Labrador Pool Exclusion

FACT: Primary suppliers may exclude from their gasoline or diesel pool any volume produced or imported into Newfoundland and Labrador and sold or delivered for use in that province, subject to maintaining records establishing that the conditions were met. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 6(2), 7(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 12C. Pool Subtraction — Remote Areas, Marine Non-Canadian Voyages, Space Heating

FACT: Fuel sold for use in a marine vessel with a non-Canadian port as destination, for non-industrial purposes in areas without NERC-standard grids or natural gas distribution, for space heating, or for electricity generation in such remote areas may be subtracted from the pool, provided records are retained before August 1 of the following year. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 8(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* For workspaces managing fuel logistics for marine operators on international voyages departing Canada, the pool-subtraction provision represents a compliance cost relief for primary-supplier clients — but only if records documenting destination port and vessel identity are maintained. Freight documentation standards should be confirmed against s. 8(2) record requirements.

### 12D. Default Carbon Intensity — 12-Month Limit

FACT: The default carbon intensity may not be used to create compliance credits for more than 12 consecutive months or more than 12 months during two consecutive compliance periods without Ministerial approval. During a pending pathway application, the default CI may be used until approval is obtained even if the period exceeds 12 months. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 75(2), 75(3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 12E. Co-processed Low-Carbon-Intensity Fuel — Specific Provisions

FACT: "co-processed low-carbon-intensity fuel means the portion of a fuel that is produced from a mixture of a petroleum feedstock and a non-petroleum feedstock that are used simultaneously in the same processing unit of a petroleum refinery or upgrader facility and that is a low-carbon-intensity fuel derived from a non-petroleum feedstock." Co-processed fuels are subject to distinct provisions under s. 1(4), with several sections (including ss. 19(1)(b)/(c), 75, 76, 94, 95, 100, 108, 123) not applying to co-processed low-carbon-intensity fuels. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 1(1), 1(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Fuel LCA Model and Specifications for Fuel LCA Model CI Calculations

FACT: The regulation defines "Fuel LCA Model" as "the fuel life-cycle assessment model that is developed by the Minister in accordance with ISO Standard 14040 and that consists of the procedures that must be followed to determine the carbon intensity of a fuel, energy source or material input using life-cycle inventories for various pathways." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: Version 3.1 of the Fuel LCA Model was released in December 2024. It "introduced conservative feedstock aggregation rules — requiring separate data for each bio-feedstock (e.g., used cooking oil, yellow grease, animal fats) and mandating the highest Carbon Intensity (CI) value when blends are used — as well as formal integration of avoided methane emissions from landfill gas and livestock manure into biogas and RNG CI calculations. It also standardized fugitive-emissions metering for CNG, LNG, and renewable gas variants, and enabled precise electricity CI accounting via North American grid-mix processes." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

FACT: Version 4.0 of the Fuel LCA Model was released in January 2025. It includes "restricted pathway resubmissions to only substantive technological changes, while establishing a dedicated approval stream for novel processes such as fuel liquefaction plants. It standardized Higher Heating Values (HHVs) across all biofuel co-products, mandated distinct CI values for manure and landfill gas, and simplified manure aggregation to ease administrative burdens for RNG producers. Version 4.0 also clarified hydrogen modelling with two approved methods for Steam Methane Reforming and Autothermal Reforming, recognized rail electrification as an eligible credit-generating activity beginning in 2025, and applied uniform fugitive-emissions factors for CNG/LNG infrastructure." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Operational implication:* Workspaces involved in the import or logistics of biofuels, RNG, or hydrogen into Canada — particularly as agents for registered creators or foreign suppliers — face updated feedstock documentation and data requirements under Model v3.1 and v4.0. Separate CI values per feedstock (not blended averages) must now be supported by supplier documentation.

### Methods for Verification and Certification

FACT: The regulation defines "Methods for Verification and Certification" as "the document entitled Methods for Verification and Certification — Clean Fuel Regulations that is developed and published by the Minister." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* The Methods for Verification and Certification sets out verification body requirements, outsourcing limits, and site-visit protocols. Workspaces that act as agents for registered creators or that have verification obligations delegated through contract must understand the Methods document as a binding incorporated reference.

### Default Carbon Intensity Schedule (Schedule 6)

FACT: The default carbon intensity for fuels where a specific pathway is not approved is: 80 gCO₂e/MJ for 2022 and 2023; 79 gCO₂e/MJ for 2024; 78 gCO₂e/MJ for 2025; 77 gCO₂e/MJ for 2026; 76 gCO₂e/MJ for 2027; 74 gCO₂e/MJ for 2028; 73 gCO₂e/MJ for 2029; and 72 gCO₂e/MJ for 2030 and following years. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, Schedule 6, s. 1, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "The default carbon intensity referred to in paragraph (1)(a) must not be used to create compliance credits for a period of more than 12 consecutive months or more than 12 months during two consecutive compliance periods, unless the Minister, at the written request of the registered creator, approves the use of that carbon intensity for any longer period specified by the Minister." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 75(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Workspaces acting as registered creators or importing low-carbon-intensity fuels on behalf of credit-generating clients must track which CI basis — default or Fuel LCA Model approved — is in use, as the 12-month limit on default CI use constrains credit-creation capacity for fuels without an approved pathway.

### Digital Compliance Tracking — CATS

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "Compliance managed via the Credit and Tracking System (CATS), a digital platform handling credit issuance, trading, and reporting." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

**Action:** For workspaces considering registered-creator status or acting as agent for registered creators, assess CATS access and integration requirements — specifically whether current TMS/ERP systems can interface with CATS or whether manual report compilation will be required.

*Operational implication:* CATS is the mandatory platform for credit issuance and trading. Workspaces without CATS access cannot execute credit transfers or receive credits. This is a prerequisite for any credit-market participation.

### Electronic Reporting

FACT: "A person who is required by these Regulations to submit a report or send a notice to the Minister must do so electronically in the form specified by the Minister and the report or notice must bear the signature of the person's authorized agent." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 164(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "If the Minister has not specified an electronic form or it is impractical for the person to submit the report or send the notice electronically because of circumstances beyond their control, the person must submit or send a paper version of the report or notice, signed by their authorized agent, in the form specified by the Minister or, if no form has been specified, in any reasonable form." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 164(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Measurement Devices

FACT: "A person who is required by these Regulations to record any volume or quantity must determine that volume or quantity (a) by using one or more measurement devices that meet the requirements of the Weights and Measures Act and the regulations made under that Act; (b) in accordance with a measurement standard or method that is appropriate for the determination and cited in the Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards, published by the American Petroleum Institute; or (c) in accordance with any applicable emission-reduction quantification method established under subsection 31(1) or 32(1)." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 161(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Monitoring Plan

FACT: "A person who is having an application or a report verified must prepare a monitoring plan, keep it up to date and submit it with the application or the report to the verification body." The monitoring plan must contain the information referred to in Schedule 21. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 136(1)-(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Workspaces pursuing registered-creator status for any credit category must develop and maintain a Schedule 21-compliant monitoring plan covering data sources, measurement devices, data management controls, and calculation methodologies. This is a standing document obligation that persists through the life of credit-generating activity.

### Feedstock Chain-of-Custody Documentation

FACT: For feedstocks referred to in s. 46(1)(b) or (c), a registered creator or foreign supplier must ensure declarations are made by every person who possesses, processes, mixes, or divides feedstock quantities at least once every year, and must retain those declarations along with material-balance records (s. 57(2)). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 57(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* For workspaces handling low-carbon-intensity fuel logistics — particularly import of biofuels — the feedstock declaration and chain-of-custody system requires supplier-level documentation that flows through transport and customs records. Logistics management systems must be capable of capturing and retaining feedstock origin, quantity, and declaration data per the s. 58 templates.

### Regulation Identity and Effective Date

FACT: The Clean Fuel Regulations were registered as SOR/2022-140 on June 21, 2022, and came into force on the day on which they were registered. *Source: Canada Gazette, Part II, Volume 156, Number 14: Clean Fuel Regulations, Government of Canada, July 6, 2022. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

FACT: "Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a fuel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada before July 1, 2023," meaning the carbon-intensity reduction obligation on primary suppliers' pools of gasoline and diesel took effect from July 1, 2023. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 5(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**effective_date slot:** FACT: The Regulations came into force on June 21, 2022 (the day of registration), with the substantive carbon-intensity reduction requirement on primary suppliers beginning July 1, 2023. *Source: Canada Gazette, Part II, Volume 156, Number 14: Clean Fuel Regulations, Government of Canada, July 6, 2022. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

### Jurisdictional Scope

**jurisdictional_scope slot:** FACT: The Regulations apply to gasoline and diesel produced in Canada or imported into Canada, with obligations falling on "primary suppliers" as defined. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 1(1), 4, 5, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: The CFR were made under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 and the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act. *Source: Canada Gazette, Part II, Volume 156, Number 14, Government of Canada, July 6, 2022. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

### Plain-Language Summary

FACT: "The Clean Fuel Regulations require liquid fossil fuel (gasoline and diesel) suppliers to gradually reduce the carbon intensity – or the amount of pollution – from the fuels they produce and sell for use in Canada over time, leading to a decrease of approximately 15% (below 2016 levels) in the carbon intensity of gasoline and diesel used in Canada by 2030." *Source: What are the Clean Fuel Regulations?, Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), Canada.ca. https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/managing-pollution/energy-production/fuel-regulations/clean-fuel-regulations/about.html

FACT: The Regulations establish a compliance credit market whereby the annual carbon intensity reduction requirement could be met via three main categories of credit-creating actions: "(1) actions that reduce the CI of the fossil fuel throughout its lifecycle, (2) supplying low-carbon fuels, and (3) supplying fuel and energy in advanced vehicle technologies." *Source: CEPA Registry – Clean Fuel Regulations (SOR/2022-140), Environment and Climate Change Canada. https://pollution-waste.canada.ca/environmental-protection-registry/regulations/view?Id=1170

### Why the Workspace Profile Is Relevant

Workspaces operating in freight forwarding, import logistics, and supply chain intermediary roles on Canadian trade lanes intersect with the CFR in three ways:

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that import diesel-powered trucking, reefer, or aviation fuel-consuming shipments into Canada may face cost pass-through from primary suppliers who carry compliance credit costs — particularly as the carbon-intensity reduction trajectory steepens annually toward 2030.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces acting as importer of record or logistics agent for biofuels, renewable natural gas, sustainable aviation fuel, or low-carbon-intensity fuels entering Canada may be adjacent to the credit-creation system as registered creators or foreign suppliers — roles that carry distinct registration and reporting obligations.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a workspace operating as freight forwarder, customs broker, or importer of record for clients qualifies as a "primary supplier" (defined as a person who owns, leases, operates, controls or manages a fuel production facility in Canada at which gasoline or diesel is produced, or who imports gasoline or diesel into Canada) under s. 1(1) of the Regulations is a legal determination requiring counsel review. FACT: The regulation defines "primary supplier" as "a person who (a) owns, leases, operates, controls or manages a fuel production facility in Canada at which gasoline or diesel is produced; or (b) imports gasoline or diesel into Canada." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Credit Market Performance Data

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "In 2024, the CFR market generated 7.9 million t CO₂e in credits (excluding CC1 credits and electricity credits), while incurring 12.3 million t CO₂e in deficits." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Analytical inference:* A structural deficit (12.3 Mt CO₂e demand versus 7.9 Mt CO₂e supply, excluding CC1 and electricity credits) in 2024 indicates upward price pressure on credit values through the compliance period, consistent with the observed average price increase from CAD $127 (2023) to CAD $157 (2024). As the annual reduction requirement deepens toward 14 gCO₂e/MJ by 2030, this structural gap is likely to persist unless credit supply from low-carbon fuel imports, EV charging, and emission-reduction projects expands proportionally.

FACT: In 2023, total credit creation reached 11.3 million t CO₂e across all categories, with Compliance Category 2 (low-carbon fuel supply) dominating at 6.8 million t CO₂e, followed by historical RFR rollover credits at 2.77 million t CO₂e and Category 3 credits at 625,930 t CO₂e. *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "In 2024, the market expanded with 347 credit transactions transferring 3.33 million t CO₂e, and an average credit price of CAD 157. Prices reached CAD 166 in Q2 but decreased to CAD 149.24 by Q4 as credit supply increased. Approximately 5 million credits were exchanged in bundled fuel-supply agreements at near-zero prices." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

### Comparator Jurisdictions

FACT: British Columbia has a Low Carbon Fuel Standard that "aims to achieve a 20% reduction in fuel carbon intensity by 2030." California has a Low Carbon Fuel Standard requiring "a 20% reduction in transportation fuel carbon intensity by 2030." Oregon's Clean Fuels Program requires "a 10% reduction in transportation fuel carbon intensity in 10 years." The EU requires fuel suppliers to reduce carbon intensity by 6% for transportation fuels. *Source: What are the Clean Fuel Regulations?, Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canada.ca. https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/managing-pollution/energy-production/fuel-regulations/clean-fuel-regulations/about.html

*Industry interpretation:* The CFR's 15% reduction by 2030 is more ambitious by reduction percentage than the EU (6%) and Oregon (10%), and comparable in ambition to California and British Columbia (both targeting 20% but over a longer or independently-structured trajectory). The comparator experience — particularly British Columbia's longer-running program — suggests that fuel-cost pass-through to commercial logistics customers is an established market practice in similar regimes.

### Fuel LCA Model Version Trajectory and RNG Market

*Analytical inference:* FACT: RNG volumes rose 417% in 2024 to 137 million cubic metres. HDRD produced 2.11 million t CO₂e credits with a CI drop of 37% to 41 gCO₂e/MJ. Ethanol CI decreased by 20% to 41 gCO₂e/MJ in 2024. *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Analytical inference:* The sharp growth in RNG volumes (417% year-on-year) and improving CI values for both ethanol and HDRD indicate accelerating commercial investment in Category 2 credit supply. Workspaces with existing logistics relationships in agricultural supply chains, waste processing, or renewable-fuel import may be positioned to facilitate feedstock or fuel flows that support registered creators — a potential service offering as the credit market deepens.

### 8A. Carbon-Intensity Reduction Requirement — Primary Suppliers

FACT: "For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, a primary supplier's pool — as determined in accordance with section 8 — of a liquid fossil fuel that is set out in column 1 of the table to this subsection must not have a carbon intensity that is greater than the corresponding limit set out in column 2 for the corresponding compliance period." Per the table to s. 5(1):

| Year | Gasoline limit (gCO₂e/MJ) | Diesel limit (gCO₂e/MJ) |
|------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| 2023 | 91.5 | 89.5 |
| 2024 | 90.0 | 88.0 |
| 2025 | 88.5 | 86.5 |
| 2026 | 87.0 | 85.0 |
| 2027 | 85.5 | 83.5 |
| 2028 | 84.0 | 82.0 |
| 2029 | 82.5 | 80.5 |
| 2030 and after | 81.0 | 79.0 |

*Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 5(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Calculation basis:** FACT: The reduction requirement per compliance period is calculated by the formula: CI_diff × (Q × D) × 10⁻⁶, where CI_diff is the difference between the baseline carbon intensity (95 gCO₂e/MJ for gasoline; 93 gCO₂e/MJ for diesel) and the applicable limit for the compliance period; Q is the volume of the pool for the compliance period in cubic metres as determined under s. 8; and D is the energy density elected by the primary supplier from Schedule 2 or the Specifications for Fuel LCA Model CI Calculations. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 9, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**primary_deadline slot:** FACT: Primary suppliers carrying a compliance deficit as of July 31 of the year following a compliance period must comply with total reduction requirements and volumetric requirements "no later than the December 15 that follows the end of a compliance period" under s. 14(4). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 14(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 8B. Volumetric Requirements

FACT: "For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, at least 5% of the volume of a primary supplier's pool of gasoline — as determined in accordance with section 8 — must, for each compliance period, be displaced by an equivalent volume of a gasoline replacement." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 6(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, at least 2% of the volume of a primary supplier's pool of diesel — as determined in accordance with section 8 — must, for each compliance period, be displaced by an equivalent volume of a diesel replacement." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 7(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Newfoundland and Labrador carve-out:** FACT: "For the purposes of subsection (1), the primary supplier may, for a compliance period, subtract from their pool of gasoline determined in accordance with section 8 any volume of gasoline that, during the compliance period, the primary supplier produced in or imported into Newfoundland and Labrador and sold or delivered for use in that province, if the primary supplier records information that establishes that the volume of gasoline met those conditions." The equivalent provision applies to diesel (s. 7(2)). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 6(2), 7(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 8C. Pool Calculation — Inclusions and Subtractions

FACT: A primary supplier determines their pool volume from fuel "(a) produced by the primary supplier at a fuel production facility in Canada and, during the compliance period, either (i) dispatched from the fuel production facility, or (ii) used to fuel a vehicle or other mobile equipment at the fuel production facility; or (b) imported by the primary supplier into Canada during the compliance period." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 8(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: A primary supplier may subtract from their pool any volume of fuel sold or delivered: (a) for a use other than combustion; (b) for use in a marine vessel with a non-Canadian port as its destination; (c) for non-industrial purposes in a geographic area served by neither an NERC-standard electrical distribution network nor a natural gas distribution system; (d) for the purpose of space heating; or (e) for electricity generation in a geographic area served by neither NERC-standard networks nor a natural gas distribution system — subject to recording before August 1 of the following calendar year. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 8(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* For workspaces managing fuel logistics on behalf of marine operators or remote-area clients, the pool-subtraction provisions in s. 8(2)(b)-(e) may be relevant to primary supplier clients' compliance calculations — requiring that delivery-destination and end-use records be captured and retained.

### 8D. Credit Creation — Three Compliance Categories

**Category 1 — Emission-Reduction Projects:**
FACT: "A registered creator may create a compliance credit in respect of the liquid class" by carrying out a CO₂e-emission-reduction project described in s. 30 (reduction, sequestration, or use of CO₂e emissions across the fuel lifecycle, or production of co-processed low-carbon-intensity fuel), recognised under ss. 35(1), 36(1), 37(3), 39(1), or 40(3). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 19(1)(a), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Category 2 — Supply of Low-Carbon-Intensity Fuels:**
FACT: A registered creator may create credits by importing or producing in Canada a quantity of low-carbon-intensity fuel (in the liquid state at standard conditions) that is used or sold for use as a fuel in Canada, meets requirements of s. 56, and is one referred to in s. 94. Credit formula: CI_diff × (Q × D) × 10⁻⁶ where CI_diff is the difference between the reference carbon intensity for the liquid class (Schedule 1, item 1) and the carbon intensity of the low-carbon-intensity fuel. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 19(1)(b)-(c), 94(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Category 3 — Supply of Fuel or Energy to Advanced Vehicles:**
FACT: A registered creator may create credits by displacing liquid-class fuel use with propane, CNG, LNG, renewable propane, compressed/liquefied renewable natural gas, renewable propane or renewable natural gas for vehicles (ss. 98–100), electricity for electric vehicles via charging-site hosts or charging-network operators (ss. 101–102), or hydrogen at hydrogen fuelling stations (s. 104). *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 19(1)(d), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: Credit creation for residential and public EV charging by charging-network operators requires that "all of the revenue that they receive from the transfer of compliance credits created under that section during all previous compliance periods is used within the time limit set out in subsection (3) for the purpose of carrying out, in Canada, either of the following activities: (a) expanding electric vehicle charging infrastructure … or (b) reducing the cost of electric vehicle ownership through financial incentives." Revenue from transferred credits must be used "no later than the second anniversary of the end of the compliance period during which the compliance credit is transferred." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 103(1), (3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 8E. Credit Use — Timelines and Limits

FACT: "A primary supplier must, no later than the July 31 that follows the end of a compliance period, use the compliance credits that are in their accounts opened under section 28, until (a) the reduction requirement is satisfied for that compliance period; or (b) no such compliance credits remain in those accounts." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 13(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: Limits on credit use from registered emission-reduction funding programs: "The primary supplier must ensure that the total number of compliance credits created under subsection 19(2) … does not exceed 10% of the primary supplier's total reduction requirement." Similarly, credits from the gaseous-fuel account (s. 28(b)) are capped at 10% of total reduction requirements; and credits created under a generic quantification method are capped at 10% of total reduction requirements. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 15(1)-(3), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 8F. Credit Clearance Mechanism

FACT: The Credit Clearance Mechanism allows deficit holders to purchase credits from participants who have pledged credits, at a price not exceeding the CPI-indexed $300 ceiling. A primary supplier who has not satisfied its total reduction requirement by July 31 must acquire, by transfer through the clearance mechanism, credits determined by the formula C × (R_p ÷ R_t) capped at its shortfall, where C is total pledged credits, R_p is the primary supplier's shortfall, and R_t is the aggregate shortfall of all primary suppliers. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 112(2), 112(3), 112(5), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "The CFR credit market is administered via the Credit and Tracking System (CATS), a digital platform handling credit issuance, trading, and reporting." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

### 8G. Deferral of Reduction Requirements

FACT: "A primary supplier may, no later than the December 15 that follows the end of a compliance period, defer satisfaction of their reduction requirements for that compliance period by any number of compliance credits that does not exceed the greater of zero and the result of the formula 10% x R_current − R_deferred." Conditions: (a) the Minister has sent a no-clearance-mechanism notice or the primary supplier has acquired required credits through the clearance mechanism; and (b) the primary supplier has created enough credits by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program to satisfy 10% of total reduction requirements. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 16(1), 16(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "A primary supplier who defers under subsection (1) a portion of their reduction requirements for a compliance period must satisfy the deferred portion no later than the December 15 that follows the fifth anniversary of the end of that compliance period." Each December 16 following a deferred compliance period, the deferred portion is multiplied by 1.05. *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 16(3), 17, Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### 8H. Penalty Summary

**penalty_summary slot:** FACT: The regulation was made in part under subsection 5(1) of the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act. *Source: Canada Gazette, Part II, Volume 156, Number 14, Government of Canada, July 6, 2022. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

FACT: The IETA brief confirms "Administrative penalties are imposed under Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Specific penalty quantum amounts per violation not available from primary sources within the corpus as of this brief's generation date.* The Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act and the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Regulations (amended by s. 173 of the CFR) set the penalty framework; exact amounts require review of those instruments. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the workspace should obtain current EVAMPA schedule amounts from counsel or directly from ECCC.

### Q1: Is the workspace a "primary supplier" within the statutory definition?

FACT: The definition requires the person to own, lease, operate, control or manage a fuel production facility in Canada producing gasoline or diesel, OR to import gasoline or diesel into Canada (s. 1(1)).

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether import activity conducted as freight forwarder, customs broker, or logistics agent — where title to the fuel may vest with a client — satisfies "imports gasoline or diesel into Canada" for the primary-supplier definition requires counsel review.

### Q2: Does the 400 m³ threshold exemption apply?

FACT: "A primary supplier who produces in Canada or imports into Canada a volume of less than 400 m³ of gasoline or a volume of less than 400 m³ of diesel during a compliance period is exempt from the application of these Regulations with respect to that fuel for that compliance period." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 4(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "For greater certainty, the fuels referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (d) are not included when determining, for the purposes of subsection (1), the volume of fuel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada by a primary supplier." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 4(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether volumes handled for multiple clients aggregate toward the 400 m³ threshold under a single importer's registration, or whether each client's volume is assessed separately, requires counsel review.

### Q3: Are there excluded fuel types?

FACT: "These Regulations do not apply in respect of gasoline or diesel that is (a) aviation gasoline; (b) exported from Canada; (c) used for scientific research, other than research on consumer preferences in respect of various properties of fuels or market research; or (d) sold or delivered for the purpose of supplying the engine of a vehicle, including a marine vessel, that is used exclusively for competition." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 4(2), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* Aviation gasoline is expressly excluded from the regulation. Workspaces handling aviation gasoline — as distinct from jet fuel or SAF — should confirm fuel classification. Standard aviation turbine fuel (Jet A/A-1) is not named as excluded in s. 4(2); its regulatory status is a separate threshold question.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether jet fuel (Jet A/A-1) falls within the definition of "gasoline" or "diesel" under the Regulations, and therefore within scope, requires counsel review of the definitions and classification standards referenced in s. 1(1).

### Q4: What compliance periods apply?

FACT: The regulation defines "compliance period" as: "(a) the period that begins on the day on which these Regulations are registered and ends on December 31, 2022; (b) the period that begins on January 1, 2023 and ends on June 30, 2023; (c) the period that begins on July 1, 2023 and ends on December 31, 2023; or (d) after December 31, 2023, each calendar year." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Q5: What is the "low-carbon-intensity fuel" definition that governs credit creation?

FACT: "low-carbon-intensity fuel means a liquid or gaseous fuel that is not a fuel in the liquid class or gaseous class and that has a carbon intensity, for the compliance period during which the fuel was produced or imported, that does not exceed (a) 90% of the reference carbon intensity set out for that compliance period in item 1, column 2, of Schedule 1, in the case of a fuel that is in the liquid state at standard conditions." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

---

### Defined Roles in the Regulation

The CFR creates four primary compliance-relevant roles:

**Primary Supplier:** FACT: Defined as "a person who (a) owns, leases, operates, controls or manages a fuel production facility in Canada at which gasoline or diesel is produced; or (b) imports gasoline or diesel into Canada." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Registered Creator:** FACT: Defined as "a person registered with the Minister in accordance with subsection 25(1)," being a person who "wishes to create compliance credits under subsection 19(1) or section 20 or under an agreement referred to in section 21." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, ss. 1(1), 25(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Foreign Supplier:** FACT: Defined as "the owner of a facility outside Canada at which a low-carbon-intensity fuel is produced or the person who leases, operates, controls or manages such a facility." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

**Carbon-Intensity Contributor:** FACT: Defined as "a person who applies for the approval of a carbon intensity under subsection 80(1) for a set of activities carried out over the life cycle of a fuel in the liquid class or a low-carbon-intensity fuel with the intention to transfer the approved carbon intensity to a registered creator or foreign supplier or to another carbon-intensity contributor." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

### Workspace Role Placement

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a workspace operating in freight forwarding, import logistics, or third-party logistics roles qualifies as a primary supplier, registered creator, foreign supplier, or carbon-intensity contributor under the Regulations depends on the specific contractual and operational structure of each transaction and requires counsel review.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that import, handle, or arrange logistics for low-carbon-intensity fuels (biofuels, renewable natural gas, sustainable aviation fuel, hydrogen, renewable propane) for clients on Canadian trade lanes may have a pathway to registered-creator status and credit generation — a commercial revenue opportunity as well as a compliance matter.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that are not primary suppliers but procure Canadian road fuel, ocean bunkers, or air fuel from primary suppliers within Canada will experience the regulation indirectly through fuel surcharges and price adjustments — the mechanism being that primary suppliers pass compliance costs through commercial fuel pricing.

FACT: As of May 31, 2024, "a total of 202 organizations have registered under various roles, including 8 primary suppliers, 97 registered creators, 54 foreign suppliers, 26 Primary Supplier/Registered Creator and 9 verification bodies." *Source: IETA Business Brief — Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

Application Marginal note: Exemption — primary suppliers 4 (1) A primary supplier who produces in Canada or imports into Canada a volume of less than 400 m 3 of gasoline or a volume of less than 400 m 3 of diesel during a compliance period is exempt from the application of these Regulations with respect to that fuel for that compliance period. Marginal note: Non-application — certain fuels (2) These Regulations do not apply in respect of gasoline or diesel that is (a) aviation gasoline; (b) exported from Canada; (c) used for scientific research, other than research on consumer preferences in respect of various properties of fuels or market research; or (d) sold or delivered for the purpose of supplying the engine of a vehicle, including a marine vessel, that is used exclusively for competition. Marginal note: Exception (3) However, a primary supplier who, during a compliance period, produces in Canada or imports into Canada a volume of 400 m 3 or more of gasoline or diesel must record the volume of every fuel referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (d) that is produced or imported during that compliance period and must include that information in the compliance report submitted to the Minister under section 127. Marginal note: Clarification (4) For greater certainty, the fuels referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (d) are not included when determining, for the purposes of subsection (1), the volume of fuel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada by a primary supplier. Requirements for Liquid Fuels Carbon-Intensity Limits Marginal note: Requirement — carbon intensity 5 (1) For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, a primary supplier’s pool — as determined in accordance with section 8 — of a liquid fossil fuel that is set out in column 1 of the table to this subsection must not have a carbon intensity that is greater than the corresponding limit set out in column 2 for the corresponding compliance period. TABLE Fuel Carbon-Intensity Limits Column 1 Column 2 Limit for Each Compliance Period (gCO 2 e/MJ) Item Liquid Fossil Fuel 2023 2024 2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 and after 1 Gasoline 91.5 90.0 88.5 87.0 85.5 84.0 82.5 81.0 2 Diesel 89.5 88.0 86.5 85.0 83.5 82.0 80.5 79.0 Marginal note: Lowering of carbon intensity (2) A primary supplier must comply with subsection (1) with respect to a fuel for a compliance period by lowering the carbon intensity of their pool of that fuel for that compliance period by an amount that is equal to the difference between the baseline carbon intensity for that fuel and the limit set out in the table to subsection (1) for that fuel and that compliance period. The carbon intensity must be lowered by using compliance credits in accordance with section 11 to satisfy the reduction requirement for that compliance period. Marginal note: Baseline carbon intensity (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), the baseline carbon intensity of gasoline is 95 gCO 2 e/MJ and the baseline carbon intensity of diesel is 93 gCO 2 e/MJ. Marginal note: Non-application (4) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a fuel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada before July 1, 2023. Marginal note: Volumetric requirement — gasoline 6 (1) For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, at least 5% of the volume of a primary supplier’s pool of gasoline — as determined in accordance with section 8 — must, for each compliance period, be displaced by an equivalent volume of a gasoline replacement. Marginal note: Exception — Newfoundland and Labrador (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the primary supplier may, for a compliance period, subtract from their pool of gasoline determined in accordance with section 8 any volume of gasoline that, during the compliance period, the primary supplier produced in or imported into Newfoundland and Labrador and sold or delivered for use in that province, if the primary supplier records information that establishes that the volume of gasoline met those conditions. Marginal note: Non-application (3) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of gasoline that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada before July 1, 2023. Marginal note: Volumetric requirement — diesel 7 (1) For the purposes of section 139 of the Act, at least 2% of the volume of a primary supplier’s pool of diesel — as determined in accordance with section 8 — must, for each compliance period, be displaced by an equivalent volume of a diesel replacement. Marginal note: Exception — Newfoundland and Labrador (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the primary supplier may, for a compliance period, subtract from their pool of diesel determined in accordance with section 8 any volume of diesel that, during the compliance period, the primary supplier produced in or imported into Newfoundland and Labrador and sold or delivered for use in that province, if the primary supplier records information that establishes that the volume of diesel met those conditions. Marginal note: Non-application (3) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of diesel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada before July 1, 2023. Marginal note: Pool of liquid fuel — volume 8 (1) A primary supplier must, for each compliance period, determine the total volume, expressed in cubic metres, of their pool of gasoline or diesel, as the case may be, that was (a) produced by the primary supplier at a fuel production facility in Canada and, during the compliance period, either (i) dispatched from the fuel production facility, or (ii) used to fuel a vehicle or other mobile equipment at the fuel production facility; or (b) imported by the primary supplier into Canada during the compliance period. Marginal note: Subtraction from pool (2) However, a primary supplier may, for each compliance period, subtract from their pool of gasoline or diesel, as the case may be, any volume of that fuel, if the primary supplier, before the August 1 of the calendar year that follows the end of the compliance period, records information that establishes that the volume of fuel met any of the following conditions during the compliance period: (a) it was sold or delivered for a use other than combustion; (b) it was sold or delivered for use in a marine vessel that had a non-Canadian port as its destination; (c) it was sold or delivered for use for non-industrial purposes in a geographic area that is served by neither an electrical distribution network that is subject to the standards of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation nor a natural gas distribution system; (d) it was sold or delivered for the purpose of space heating; (e) it was sold or delivered for use in the generation of electricity in a geographic area that is served by neither an electrical distribution network that is subject to the standards of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation nor a natural gas distribution system. Reduction Requirement Marginal note: Reduction in tonnes 9 The carbon intensity of a pool of gasoline or diesel for a compliance period is considered to be lowered for the purposes of subsection 5(2) if the number of tonnes of CO 2 e released over the life cycle of that fuel is reduced by the value of the reduction requirement for that compliance period, as determined by the formula CI diff × (Q × D) × 10 -6 where CI diff is the difference, expressed in gCO 2 e/MJ, between the baseline carbon intensity of that fuel, as set out in subsection 5(3), and the limit for that fuel for that compliance period, as set out in column 2 of the table to subsection 5(1); Q is the volume of that pool for the compliance period, as determined in accordance with section 8 and expressed in cubic metres; and D is, at the election of the primary supplier, the energy density of the fuel as set out in column 2 of Schedule 2 or as set out in the Specifications for Fuel LCA Model CI Calculations. Registration as Primary Supplier Marginal note: Registration report 10 (1) A primary supplier must register with the Minister by submitting a registration report to the Minister that contains the information referred to in sections 1 to 3 of Schedule 3 no later than 45 days after the day on which they have produced in Canada or imported into Canada, during a compliance period, a total volume of 400 m 3 or more of gasoline or a total volume of 400 m 3 or more of diesel. Marginal note: Exception — registration within 90 days (2) However, the registration report may be submitted at any time during the period that begins on the day on which these Regulations are registered and ends 90 days after that day. Marginal note: Change of information (3) If there are any changes in the information referred to in section 1 of Schedule 3 that is provided in the registration report, the primary supplier must send a notice to the Minister that provides the updated information within 30 days after the day on which the change occurs. Marginal note: Notice of cancellation (4) A primary supplier who is not required by subsection (1) to be registered for a given compliance period and who has complied with the requirements set out in these Regulations for all of the previous compliance periods, including the volumetric requirements set out in subsections 6(1) and 7(1) and the reduction requirement, may cancel their registration as a primary supplier by sending a notice to that effect to the Minister. Marginal note: Cancellation by Minister (5) If, after receiving the notice referred to in subsection (4), the Minister is satisfied that the primary supplier has complied with these Regulations for all previous compliance periods, the Minister must (a) if the primary supplier is not a registered creator, cancel any compliance credits in their accounts opened under section 28; (b) cancel their registration as a primary supplier; and (c) send a notice to the primary supplier informing them that their registration has been cancelled. Marginal note: Clarification (6) For greater certainty, subsection (1) applies to a primary supplier whose registration was cancelled by the Minister under subsection (5). Compliance Credits Use Marginal note: Satisfaction of reduction requirement 11 (1) A primary supplier must use the compliance credits that they create under sections 19 and 20, or that are transferred to them under the compliance-credit transfer system, to satisfy the total reduction requirement. Marginal note: Deemed reduction (2) The use of one compliance credit by a primary supplier for gasoline or diesel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada during a compliance period is deemed to reduce by one tonne the quantity of CO 2 e released over the life cycle of that fuel during that compliance period. Marginal note: Prior creation of provisional credit (3) The primary supplier must use only the compliance credits that are created as provisional compliance credits before the end of a compliance period or the compliance credits that they create under subsection 19(2) to satisfy the reduction requirement for that compliance period. Marginal note: Cancellation after use (4) The Minister must cancel a compliance credit immediately after it is used. Marginal note: Deemed compliance — gasoline 12 (1) For the purposes of subsection 6(1), a compliance credit that was created under paragraph 19(1)(a), (b) or (c) by producing in Canada or importing into Canada a volume of a gasoline replacement, and that is used by a primary supplier in accordance with section 11 for a compliance period, is deemed to displace, for that compliance period, the use of an equivalent volume of the primary supplier’s pool of gasoline. Marginal note: Deemed compliance — diesel (2) For the purposes of subsection 7(1), a compliance credit that was created under paragraph 19(1)(a), (b) or (c) by producing in Canada or importing into Canada a volume of a diesel replacement, and that was used by a primary supplier in accordance with section 11 for a compliance period, is deemed to displace, for that compliance period, the use of an equivalent volume of the primary supplier’s pool of diesel. Marginal note: Prior creation of provisional credit (3) The primary supplier must use only the compliance credits that are created as provisional compliance credits before the end of a compliance period to comply with the volumetric requirements set out in subsections 6(1) and 7(1) for that compliance period. Marginal note: July 31 — gasoline 13 (1) For the purposes of subsection 12(1), a primary supplier must, no later than the July 31 that follows the end of a compliance period, use — in accordance with subsection 12(3) — the compliance credits that are in their account opened under paragraph 28(a), until (a) the volumetric requirement set out in subsection 6(1) is met for that compliance period; or (b) no such compliance credits remain in that account. Marginal note: July 31 — diesel (2) For the purposes of subsection 12(2), a primary supplier must, no later than the July 31 that follows the end of a compliance period, use — in accordance with subsection 12(3) — the compliance credits that are in their account opened under paragraph 28(a), until (a) the volumetric requirement set out in subsection 7(1) is met for that compliance period; or (b) no such compliance credits remain in that account. Marginal note: July 31 — contribution to funding program (3) For the purposes of section 11 and subject to subsection 15(1), a primary supplier must, no later than the July 31 that follows the end of a compliance period, use all of the compliance credits that they created by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program in accordance with paragraph 118(1)(a) to satisfy the reduction requirement for that compliance period. Marginal note: July 31 — reduction requirement (4) For the purposes of section 11 and subject to subsections 15(2) and (3), a primary supplier must, no later than the July 31 that follows the end of a compliance period, use the compliance credits that are in their accounts opened under section 28, until (a) the reduction requirement is satisfied for that compliance period; or (b) no such compliance credits remain in those accounts. Marginal note: Choice of compliance credits (5) Subject to subsections (1) and (2), if the circumstances described in paragraph (4)(a) occur before the circumstances described in paragraph (4)(b), the primary supplier must satisfy the reduction requirement by using compliance credits that are chosen by them and indicated in the report submitted under subsection 127(1). Marginal note: August 1 — cancellation of credits (6) On the August 1 that follows the end of a compliance period, if any of the compliance credits referred to in subsection (3) have not been used by the primary supplier, the Minister must cancel those credits. Marginal note: Non-application — subsections (1) to (4) (7) Subsections (1) to (4) do not apply in respect of any compliance period that ends before July 1, 2023. Marginal note: December 15 — gasoline 14 (1) For the purposes of subsection 12(1), if a primary supplier, on the August 1 that follows the end of a compliance period, has not complied with the volumetric requirement set out in subsection 6(1) for that compliance period, the primary supplier must, no later than the following December 15, comply with that requirement by using the compliance credits transferred to them under section 112. Marginal note: December 15 — diesel (2) For the purposes of subsection 12(2), if a primary supplier, on the August 1 that follows the end of a compliance period, has not complied with the volumetric requirement set out in subsection 7(1) for that compliance period, the primary supplier must, no later than the following December 15, comply with that requirement by using the compliance credits transferred to them under section 112. Marginal note: Other credits (3) For the purposes of section 11 and subject to subsection 15(1), if a primary supplier, on the August 1 that follows the end of a compliance period, has not satisfied the reduction requirement for that compliance period, the primary supplier must, no later than the December 15 that follows the end of that compliance period, use the compliance credits that were transferred to them under section 112, or that they created by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program in accordance with paragraph 118(1)(b), to satisfy that reduction requirement. Marginal note: Compliance — December 15 (4) Subject to sections 16 to 18, a primary supplier must, no later than the December 15 that follows the end of a compliance period, use the compliance credits in their accounts opened under section 28 to satisfy the total reduction requirement and comply with the volumetric requirements set out in subsections 6(1) and 7(1) for that compliance period. Marginal note: December 16 — cancellation (5) On the December 16 that follows the expiry of a compliance period, if any of the compliance credits that are referred to in subsection (3) have not been used by the primary supplier, the Minister must cancel those credits. Marginal note: Non-application — subsections (1) to (4) (6) Subsections (1) to (4) do not apply in respect of any compliance period that ends before July 1, 2023. Marginal note: Limits on credit use — funding program 15 (1) The primary supplier must ensure that the total number of compliance credits created under subsection 19(2) — that are used in accordance with subsections 13(3) and 14(3), paragraph 18(1)(a) and subsection 18(3) during the calendar year that follows the end of a compliance period — does not exceed 10% of the primary supplier’s total reduction requirement. Marginal note: Limit — paragraph 28(b) (2) The primary supplier must ensure that the total number of compliance credits in their account opened under paragraph 28(b) — that are used in accordance with subsection 13(4) and paragraph 18(1)(b) during the calendar year that follows the end of a compliance period — does not exceed 10% of the primary supplier’s total reduction requirement. Marginal note: Limit — generic quantification method (3) The primary supplier must ensure that the total number of compliance credits created under paragraph 19(1)(a) in respect of a project for which a generic emission-reduction quantification method is applicable — that are used in accordance with subsection 13(4) and paragraphs 18(1)(b) and (c) during the calendar year that follows the end of a compliance period — does not exceed 10% of the primary supplier’s total reduction requirement. Marginal note: Deferral of reduction requirements 16 (1) A primary supplier may, no later than the December 15 that follows the end of a compliance period, defer satisfaction of their reduction requirements for that compliance period by any number of compliance credits that does not exceed the greater of zero and the result of the formula 10% x R current − R deferred where R current is the sum of their reduction requirements in respect of gasoline and diesel for that compliance period; and R deferred is the sum of all deferred portions of the reduction requirements in respect of gasoline and diesel for previous compliance periods. Marginal note: Conditions for deferral (2) The primary supplier may defer a portion of their reduction requirements for a compliance period under subsection (1) only if (a) the Minister has sent a notice in accordance with subsection 111(2) for that compliance period or the primary supplier has acquired by transfer through the compliance-credit clearance mechanism the number of compliance credits determined in accordance with paragraph 112(5)(b) for that compliance period; and (b) the primary supplier has created enough compliance credits by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program to satisfy 10% of the total reduction requirement for that compliance period in respect of all types of fuels. Marginal note: Compliance required after five years (3) A primary supplier who defers under subsection (1) a portion of their reduction requirements for a compliance period must satisfy the deferred portion no later than the December 15 that follows the fifth anniversary of the end of that compliance period. Marginal note: Increase to deferred portion 17 On each December 16 that follows the end of a compliance period for which a portion of the reduction requirements is deferred under subsection 16(1) and that precedes the fifth anniversary of the end of that compliance period, the deferred portion of the reduction requirements is to be multiplied by 1.05. Marginal note: Reduction — July 31 18 (1) In order to reduce a deferred portion of the reduction requirements in accordance with section 11, the primary supplier must, during the period that begins on the day after a compliance period expires and ends on the July 31 that follows that day, use the following compliance credits that are in their accounts opened under section 28 and that exceed the number required to satisfy the reduction requirements for the compliance period that ended most recently: (a) subject to subsection 15(1), all of the compliance credits that they created by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program in accordance with paragraph 118(1)(a); (b) subject to subsections 15(2) and (3), any compliance credits in their account opened under paragraph 28(b); and (c) subject to subsection 15(3), any compliance credits in their account opened under paragraph 28(a). Marginal note: Election (2) If the primary supplier has more credits than the number required to satisfy the deferred portion of the reduction requirements in accordance with subsection (1), they may elect to use any number of compliance credits referred to in paragraphs (1)(b) and (c) to satisfy the deferred portion of the reduction requirements. Marginal note: Reduction — December 15 (3) Subject to subsection 15(1), if a primary supplier, on the August 1 that follows the end of a compliance period, has not satisfied the deferred portion of the reduction requirements for a previous compliance period in accordance with subsection (2), the primary supplier must, no later than the following December 15, reduce the deferred portion of the reduction requirements by using all of the compliance credits in their account opened under paragraph 28(a) — that were transferred to them through the compliance-credit clearance mechanism under section 112 or that they created by contributing to a registered emission-reduction funding program in accordance with paragraph 118(1)(b) — that exceed the number of compliance credits required to satisfy their reduction requirements for the compliance period that ended most recently. Marginal note: Multiple compliance periods (4) If a primary supplier has not satisfied the deferred portion of the reduction requirements for more than one previous compliance period, they must not use any compliance credits to reduce the deferred portion of the reduction requirements in accordance with subsection (1) or (3) for a particular compliance period unless they have satisfied the deferred portion of the reduction requirements for every compliance period that precedes that particular compliance period. Marginal note: Non-application (5) Subsections (1) to (4) do not apply before January 1, 2025.
